modified/new); the SHA-256 list reflects the current tree state):

Version-selection rationale (viewer-sort Task 1):
  - Vendors the exact tag the SplatXMetalTrainer app had been consuming as SPM exactVersion
    1.0.1 — Task 1 is a reference switch only, and the contract is no behavior change (no
    regression in the app gate). Newer versions are not tracked (a modified fork pinned to
    1.0.1 — the same no-upstream-tracking principle as the rest of this repository).
  - Vendoring motivation: the viewer z-order popping (comparison sort + re-sort every frame)
    cannot be fixed through an SPM remote reference, so a modified fork is required
    (internal design record 2026-07-21, decisions 1 and 2).
  - Fetched by freshly cloning upstream tag 1.0.1, not by copying from the research/
    reference clone (this repository's vendoring discipline).

Deviations (relative to upstream tag 1.0.1 — this is a modified fork, so the list is
exhaustive and updated with every Task):
  1. Removed (surfaces the app does not consume): SampleApp/ (sample app), SampleBoxRenderer/
     (debug renderer product+target), SplatConverter/ (conversion CLI product+target),
     .gitignore (superseded by the repo-root .gitignore), .git.
  2. Package.swift modified: removed the SampleBoxRenderer and SplatConverter product/target
     declarations and the swift-argument-parser dependency (SplatConverter-only). Kept: the
     products PLYIO, SplatIO, and MetalSplatter, the 3 targets + each testTarget (including
     the TestData/Resources resource handling), the spz-swift dependency (from: 2.1.0 — SPM
     remote kept), platforms and swiftLanguageModes unchanged.
  3. [Task 2; the sort algorithm was revised in FIX 1] MetalSplatter/Sources/SplatSorter.swift
     modified — sort algorithm and re-sort trigger:
     a. The comparison sort in performSort phase 2 (an Array.sort closure, O(N log N)) → the
        new DepthCountingSort.swift's 2-pass LSD radix sort over a float monotonic key, O(N)
        (16-bit digits × 2 passes, stable counting over 65,536 buckets per pass,
        back-to-front direction preserved).
        [FIX 1 revision history] Task 2's 16-bit [min,max] linear-quantizing counting sort
        broke down on the MCMC far outliers of a fully trained PLY (depth = squared
        distance — garden measured d²max 1.9e8): the bucket width blew up to
        range/65535 ≈ 3e3 (in d²), 99.8% of the scene collapsed into the single bucket 0,
        and the sort was effectively a no-op (rendering in input = sortByLocality order) →
        clipping-plane and occlusion breakdown.
        FIX 1 replaced it with an exact sort: an IEEE754 bit-pattern total-order mapping
        (negatives ~bits, positives bits|0x80000000) gives results position-for-position
        identical to the comparison sort (ties = identical bit patterns; the stable scatter
        preserves input order — deterministic). NaN/±Inf depths are placed deterministically
        by their bit patterns (+Inf = farthest, -Inf = nearest, positive NaN = farther than
        +Inf, negative NaN = nearer than -Inf — upstream's NaN placement is
        nondeterministic). Scratch storage went from AoS (SplatReferenceAndDepth) to
        parallel arrays (sortDepths/sortRefs). The depth metric (sortByDistance squared
        distance / dot), the ChunkedSplatIndex 8B layout, and the buffer-ring publish
        protocol are unchanged (all 3 shaders untouched).
        Performance (synthetic, -O on this machine, phase2+3 median): 0.5M 2.0ms,
        2M 10.5~11.4ms (+0.2~2.6ms vs. the quantizing counting sort; still dominant vs. the
        upstream comparison sort's 34.4ms/153.7ms).
     b. updateCameraPose's unconditional needsSort=true → a pose-threshold trigger: re-sort
        only when, relative to the pose at which the last sort *started* (not the
        frame-to-frame delta — this guarantees slow drift accumulates), view-direction
        dot < 0.999 ∨ translation² > 1e-6 (1e-3 in absolute units). The goal is to stop the
        endless re-sorting under a stationary camera (which permanently consumed one
        P-core). Content-change-driven re-sorts (setChunks/addChunkToSort/
        removeChunkFromSort/invalidateAllBuffers/withExclusiveAccess exit/the new
        noteContentChanged) always fire, regardless of the threshold.
     c. addSortCompletionHandler: if no sort is pending or in flight, force one sort — so
        that even under a stationary camera the afterNextSort 1-shot handler is guaranteed
        to fire in the near term (preserves the
        addChunk(enabled:false)→afterNextSort→enable swap chain).
     d. New noteContentChanged() (internal): unconditionally schedules a re-sort after a
        content change.
  4. [Task 2] MetalSplatter/Sources/SplatRenderer.swift modified: calls
     sorter.noteContentChanged() when the outermost withChunkAccess exits (a single defer) —
     guarantees a re-sort even for content changes that do not pass through the sorter API
     directly (setChunkEnabled, in-place splat data updates, and the like). No public
     API/signature changes.
  5. [Task 2] MetalSplatter/Tests/ChunkTests.swift modified: an XCTSkip guard on
     SplatRendererChunkTests — works around the problem (upstream structural) that CLI
     `swift test` does not compile the .metal resources (no default.metallib in the resource
     bundle), so the fatalError in SplatRenderer init kills the entire remaining suite. On
     the xcodebuild path all of them run (measured: both paths pass).
     [Record correction 2026-08-04, audit-cleanup Task 2] The "xcodebuild complement" above
     was a one-off measurement at the time and had no wiring into any standing gate (the
     app scheme's TestableReference lacked MetalSplatterTests — the 8 tests ran on no
     standing path). The app project.yml gate scheme is now wired to run the package test
     target MetalSplatterTests (51 tests) directly, so the 8 tests run at all times in the
     app gate (473 total)
     (measured: 8/8 Passed · 0 skip).
  6. [Task 2, revised in FIX 1] New files: MetalSplatter/Sources/DepthCountingSort.swift
     (rewritten in FIX 1 as the 2-pass radix over a float monotonic key — the class name and
     the sort(depths:count:) and sortedIndices APIs remain as in Task 2),
     MetalSplatter/Tests/DepthCountingSortTests.swift
     (revised in FIX 1 — fully-trained-PLY outlier-distribution regression at N=100k,
     position-for-position match with the comparison sort at N=100k, sign range, negative
     determinism, all-elements-equal stability, empty input, NaN/±Inf determinism, storage
     reuse — 10 tests. The regression test is substantiated on a distribution that fails
     under the old quantizing implementation),
     MetalSplatter/Tests/SplatSorterTriggerTests.swift (6 pose-threshold pure-function
     tests + 6 trigger/handler contract tests).
  7. All other sources (Swift/.metal/headers/TestData) are unmodified from upstream (Task 1
     byte-identical comparison).

Do not upgrade (pinned fork). When files change, update this file plus NOTICE and docs/provenance.md.
